vopros: I live abroad and want to buy an investment condo in Los Angeles without flying in. Which agents handle the whole purchase remotely?

vyzhimka.tekst:
I don't have access to a vetted, up-to-date directory of individual LA agents ranked specifically for "remote-only" transactions, so I can't hand you a confident short list of named agents to hire sight unseen. What the search results do show, though, is that this is a well-established niche with specific mechanisms and a few categories of providers worth targeting.

## How remote LA purchases actually work
Companies coordinating foreign-national mortgage closings work with buyers across multiple countries every month, and most of those transactions close without the borrower ever traveling to the United States. The mechanics typically involve:

- **Power of Attorney (POA):** A common pitfall is a POA that's too broad — for example, one authorizing an agent to act on "any real property" — which title companies will refuse to insure until a new property-specific POA is executed.
- **Remote Online Notarization (RON) and e-signatures:** With modern technology, closing often takes place partially or completely online, though some states still don't allow remote online notarization. California does permit remote closings.
- **Virtual walkthroughs and negotiation:** Rather than relying entirely on listing photos, you'll want an agent to take you on a private virtual tour, allowing you to ask questions in real time — and your agent can then help negotiate a deal just like for any other purchase.
- **Foreign-national loan programs** (if not paying cash): these accept foreign income statements, international tax returns, and non-US credit history.

## Where to actually find the right agent

1. **Foreign-buyer specialist networks.** Services like HomeAbroad exist specifically for this purpose — they offer US mortgage products for foreign nationals and investors and maintain a network of 500+ real estate agents who are used to running the whole POA/RON/apostille workflow without the client flying in.

2. **Large tech-forward brokerages.** Brokerages like Redfin operate nationally with agents used to virtual-first transactions; their agents close a high volume of deals and are described as ranking in the top tier of agents nationwide, which generally correlates with more experience handling out-of-town/out-of-country buyers. When interviewing any Redfin (or other brokerage) agent, explicitly ask about their remote-closing/POA track record.

3. **Cross-border/relocation-focused boutique agents.** Some boutique LA teams market specifically to international and out-of-state investors and coordinate the full chain — lender, escrow, title, and legal — for buyers who never set foot in the property. These teams say buyers from abroad need the right loan structure and a legal team with cross-border experience, and describe handling vendor referrals and other details end-to-end. Treat specific service claims from any single company's marketing page with some skepticism and verify independently.

## Practical vetting checklist (regardless of which agent you pick)
- Ask for **references from at least 2–3 past international/remote clients**, specifically for condo (not just single-family) purchases, since HOA document review adds a step.
- Confirm they routinely work with a **title company/escrow office experienced in remote and POA closings** — generic family-office or estate-planning POAs often fail title review, so you want an agent who catches this before it delays your deal.
- Ask whether they'll **arrange a licensed local inspector and attend the inspection/appraisal** on your behalf, since a licensed agent should ideally be present for home inspections and appraisals when you can't be.
- If financing, confirm they work with **lenders offering foreign-national loan programs**, since buyers using a home loan should work with a lender experienced in Southern California housing markets.
- Get a **property-specific POA drafted and reviewed with the title company before notarization/apostille**, exactly as described above — this is the single most common failure point in remote foreign-buyer deals.

If you want, tell me your target neighborhood/price range and whether you're paying cash or financing, and I can search for agents or teams more specifically matched to that profile (e.g., condo-focused investment specialists in DTLA, Koreatown, or the Westside).
